explanation: Sort meetings by start and compare consecutive intervals. A meeting starting before the previous one ends requires a second room.
timeComplexity: O(n log n) time for n meetings. Sorting by start dominates the n-1 adjacent comparisons.
spaceComplexity: O(n) auxiliary space. A separate sorted sequence holds n interval records or references.
attribution: Original EPI Practice C# implementation, reusing and refining the repository-authored Blind75 algorithm fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: After sorting by start, any overlap involves an adjacent conflicting pair: if a meeting starts before an earlier meeting ends, then the latest preceding start also witnesses some overlap when all preceding adjacent pairs were compatible. Checking each consecutive end/start boundary therefore detects exactly whether one person can attend all meetings.
walkthrough: For meetings [0,2],[2,5],[6,9], the second begins exactly when the first ends, and the third begins after the second ends. No positive-duration overlap exists, so return true.
edgeCases: An end time equal to the next start is allowed.
The input need not be sorted.
Empty or singleton schedules are always attendable.
